lanes.summary: Finch has no AI features. Data is local by default, so the core loop never waits on a server, and Help lists only gifting, good vibes and adding friends as needing a connection. A failed video says why ("check your internet connection and try again") but its only buttons are Shuffle and Start the next one, with no Retry. Help keeps a public App Status page.

lanes.summary: No AI or tracking consent was found, so this traces the closest choice: sending your data to Finch's servers through Cloud Backup. It is opt-in by creating an account, Cloud Backups has a clear "Disable Cloud Backups" button plus Advanced Data Protection and Wi-Fi-only options, and "Delete data" says it erases both device and server copies. What disabling does to copies already on the server was not observed.

lanes.summary: An account is optional, made by verifying a phone number or, for older users, email and password, and Finch otherwise runs local-only. Help covers logging in on a new device (Log In › phone/email, or Manual Backup), but no sign-out control appeared in the Settings or Profile screens observed, and wrong-code or cancelled sign-in was not seen.

lanes.summary: There is no live multi-device sync. Cloud Backup runs once every 24 hours while the app is open, so a second phone restores a snapshot rather than mirroring edits, and Help says Finch has no family plans. Friends work well: add by code, link or contacts, shared goals ("Alex shared a daily goal with you!"), Buddy up. Unfriending or leaving was not observed.
